claims.statement: dcode create_model applies its allowlist after provider inference but before credential bridging, provider profiles, and provider imports; blocked models therefore cannot cause those side effects.

dcode model construction uses provider-profile defaults beneath config provider and per-model parameters plus credential wiring, with extra runtime or CLI kwargs winning; per-model params shallow-merge over provider-wide flat params, while capability profile overrides use a separate upstream then config then CLI key-wise precedence.

ConfigurableModelMiddleware reads runtime context per model call to swap a requested model through create_model or merge per-call model_params, and after successful parent calls persists resume and cache metadata separately so configured defaults are not replayed as session overrides.

dcode builds effective capability profiles by merging upstream metadata with config.toml profile overrides and then a CLI profile override; each later layer wins by key, and CLI fields are applied to every profile entry.

Model discovery is performed on the inference host: load_model_catalog loads the active ModelConfig, obtains allowlist-filtered availability and effective profiles, adds eligible recommended/current entries and enabled known providers, and returns a validated ModelCatalog with displayable models, profiles, provider readiness, policy provenance, and current spec.

The catalog process boundary is deliberately presentation-only: model profiles are filtered to an allowlist of scalar capability fields, provider entries expose readiness, labels and optional install extra but not credential values, and presentation_config reconstructs only provider labels and allowlist policy for the client.

Model API endpoints bind catalog and resolution to a thread workspace and inference environment: request schemas are allowlisted, main-purpose profile overrides are applied while auxiliary requests cannot carry extra kwargs, blocking discovery/construction runs in a worker thread, and workspace conflict, validation/configuration, and availability/unexpected failures map to 409, 422, and 503 respectively.

ModelMetadata validates server payload shape before updating client runtime state and serializes only model name, provider, optional context limit, unsupported modalities, and optional structured-output capability; it never serializes a model object or credentials.

ConfigurableModelMiddleware injects thread-scoped prompt-cache routing only when a user has not already supplied it: Fireworks receives prompt_cache_key plus x-session-affinity and OpenAI receives prompt_cache_key unless the resolved opt-out is disabled; a cross-provider switch away from Anthropic strips Anthropic-only cache_control settings.

Dcode owns retry at the model-node boundary so transient model failures do not replay completed tool calls; construction stamps a provider-specific budget on the model and disables known provider SDK retry loops, while CodeModelRetryMiddleware reads the stamped budget for every request so runtime switches use the replacement provider budget.

The retry loop re-raises terminal errors rather than returning an AI message, retries only classified transient errors, prefers a capped Retry-After delay over jittered exponential backoff, and applies cumulative delay guards; interactive retries emit correlated attempt and retry events so clients can mark visible partial output from a superseded attempt.

Prompt-cache checkpoint identity records request time, model spec, endpoint identity, and a narrow effective-parameter projection after a successful call; it keeps runtime resume parameters separate from configured cache identity, tracks cache read/write activity from response usage, and omits checkpoint updates for non-persisting subagent middleware.

Cache identity parameters include prompt-cache key, options, retention, and canonical reasoning effort only for OpenAI, Codex, and Anthropic; endpoint identity normalizes routing-significant HTTP endpoint components while hashing query or malformed values, and cache-policy resolution declines unsupported, cross-format, or untrusted routes.

Focused tests establish that remote pickers do not consult local provider configuration, model middleware timestamps and isolates cache activity, retry middleware handles retry budgets and transient streaming failures, and cache-expiry UI behavior is exercised independently of model-state mutation.

For a canonical environment-variable name, resolve_env_var gives a present DEEPAGENTS_CODE_ prefixed variant precedence over the canonical name; an empty prefixed value suppresses the canonical value and resolves as absent.

Stored provider credentials are applied only on the inference host, overwrite plain canonical SDK environment names, and reconcile paired endpoint variables; the implementation writes only unprefixed names so prefixed environment overrides remain authoritative, while split key/endpoint tiers are diagnostic-only and log names rather than values.

Model policy and credential failures are actionable typed configuration errors: ModelNotAllowedError reports deny-all, unmatched, or excluded allowlist cases with policy provenance, while MissingCredentialsError carries the selected provider and canonical credential-variable name when available; readiness models distinguish missing, implicit, managed, no-auth-required, and unknown auth states.

The SDK exposes orthogonal beta profile registries: ProviderProfile controls string-model construction through init_chat_model, while HarnessProfile controls prompt, tools, middleware, and default-subagent behavior after model construction; both accept provider or provider:model keys and registration layers rather than replaces existing settings.

Provider-profile resolution merges an exact model profile over its provider profile, chains pre-initialization hooks and dynamic factories base first, and lets factory output override static profile kwargs while caller kwargs retain final precedence.

Harness-profile lookup selects an exact spec before provider fallback and merges model-level and provider-level fields; create_deep_agent resolves this profile for the main model and each declarative subagent before applying prompt, tool-description, and middleware changes.

Profile bootstrap is lazy, thread-coordinated, and one-time: built-ins load by direct imports, then third-party provider and harness entry-point hooks layer on top; broken built-ins fail bootstrap while broken third-party plugins are logged and skipped.

HarnessProfileConfig is the serializable YAML/JSON subset of runtime harness profiles; it rejects runtime-only extra middleware and invalid or required-scaffolding middleware exclusions, while focused tests cover serialization, type and grammar failures, prompt composition, and fresh middleware materialization.
